phases.name: 1. Define the viewer paths
phases.description: Keep creator, viewer, and playback traffic clear while preserving the stated startup and concurrency goals.

phases.name: 2. Upload and publish verified media
phases.description: Persist the original, process asynchronously, and expose only complete renditions.

phases.name: 3. Protect and deliver playback
phases.description: Check viewing rights before issuing a manifest and use the CDN for global, adaptive delivery.

phases.name: 4. Search and personalize
phases.description: Keep profiles and watch history durable while indexing and recommendation work stays off the playback critical path.

phases.name: 5. Scale and operate the service
phases.description: Observe the slowest user paths and plan release-day capacity without inventing unprovided traffic numbers.

steps.title: Start from the brief
steps.content: The brief requires upload and storage, millions of concurrent viewers, 480p/720p/1080p/4K, adaptive bitrate playback, search and recommendations, profiles and watch history, and global delivery. It also sets startup below two seconds and calls out release peaks, multiple device types, storage efficiency, copyright, and DRM. We will distinguish the upload/processing path from the playback path so expensive work cannot block a viewer.

steps.title: Add web viewers and creators
steps.content: Web users upload and browse through HTTPS, then request a playback manifest. The same edge handles creator and viewer traffic, but authorization and rate policies differ by operation.

component.label: Web Video Client
component.description: Browser upload, search, profile, and playback experience

properties.purpose: Upload and browse videos, manage a profile, and request adaptive playback over HTTPS.

component.highlightReason: The problem explicitly requires browser support as well as media upload and viewing.

steps.title: Add mobile and connected-device clients
steps.content: Mobile and TV-class devices have different network conditions and decoder capabilities. The playback manifest must let each device select compatible renditions rather than forcing one fixed file.

component.label: Mobile & TV Clients

properties.purpose: Browse and play video on mobile and connected devices using the rendition their decoder and network can sustain.

component.highlightReason: Separate device clients make the multiple-device requirement visible without assuming identical playback behavior.

steps.title: Add the protected API entry
steps.content: The API validates uploads, profile actions, and playback-manifest requests. It applies identity, request validation, and abuse limits; it does not proxy the large video bytes.

component.label: Video API Gateway

properties.purpose: Validate upload and account requests, enforce authentication and quotas, and route manifest requests without proxying media bytes.

component.highlightReason: Separating control requests from media delivery protects the low-latency playback path.

steps.title: Connect the web client to the API
steps.content: Web upload, search, profile, and manifest operations use the protected API. Media playback will use the CDN after the rights check.

connection.label: Web API requests
connection.description: Authenticated upload, account, search, and playback-manifest requests.

steps.title: Connect mobile and TV clients
steps.content: Mobile and connected-device requests share the API contract but retain device-specific playback capabilities and credentials.

connection.label: Device API requests
connection.description: Authenticated account, search, upload, and manifest requests from mobile or TV clients.

steps.title: Keep original uploads in durable object storage
steps.content: Large source files belong in object storage, not in a synchronous application request or relational row. Use scoped upload credentials, checksums, and lifecycle tiers; retain the original as the recovery source for re-encoding.

component.label: Original Video Object Store
component.description: Durable source uploads and lifecycle-managed originals

properties.purpose: Store large immutable source files; verify upload checksums and apply retention tiers while keeping a recoverable source for reprocessing.

component.highlightReason: This directly addresses large-file storage efficiency and upload recovery.

steps.title: Upload bytes without proxying through the API
steps.content: After the gateway authorizes an upload, the client writes the media bytes to the scoped object-store destination. The service records completion only after size and checksum verification.

connection.label: Authorized direct upload
connection.description: Issue a narrowly scoped upload target; verify object size and checksum before marking the upload complete.

steps.title: Add the media metadata source of truth
steps.content: Store ownership, upload state, rights references, and processing version separately from the bytes. A media item is not playable merely because an upload object exists.

component.label: Media Metadata Store
component.description: Ownership, upload status, and processing version

properties.purpose: Own video identity, owner, rights reference, upload state, and versioned processing status; object bytes remain in object storage.

component.highlightReason: A single metadata authority makes upload completion and later publication states explicit.

steps.title: Record an upload before processing
steps.content: The gateway records the authorized media item and its source-object reference. Use an idempotency key so client retries do not create duplicate videos or processing jobs.

connection.label: Create media record
connection.description: Persist owner, source reference, rights state, and an idempotent upload operation.

steps.title: Add a durable media-processing queue
steps.content: Encoding and thumbnail work can take much longer than an API request. A durable queue absorbs upload bursts, supports bounded retries, and keeps processing status observable.

component.label: Media Processing Queue
component.description: Durable jobs for encoding and media validation

properties.purpose: Buffer media jobs independently of upload requests and isolate poison inputs with bounded retry and dead-letter handling.

component.highlightReason: Asynchronous processing protects upload latency during popular releases.

steps.title: Enqueue a versioned processing job
steps.content: Only a verified source object and committed metadata record produce an encode job. Include media ID, object version, requested rendition profile, and job version so retries are safe.

connection.label: Verified upload job
connection.description: Enqueue a versioned encode request after object verification and metadata commit.

steps.title: Add elastic transcoding workers
steps.content: Workers validate the source and create compatible 480p, 720p, 1080p, and 4K renditions. Size worker pools by media duration, codec, and priority rather than allowing one unusually large file to consume all capacity.

component.label: Transcoding Workers
component.description: Validate media and create supported rendition profiles

properties.purpose: Validate sources and create 480p, 720p, 1080p, and 4K outputs with bounded, profile-aware concurrency.

component.highlightReason: The required quality ladder is created asynchronously and can scale separately from viewers.

steps.title: Dispatch jobs to workers
steps.content: Workers claim jobs with a lease and retry using deterministic output keys. A crashed worker must not publish a partial rendition or duplicate a completed profile.

connection.label: Leased encode jobs
connection.description: At-least-once dispatch with idempotent outputs, bounded retries, and a dead-letter path.

steps.title: Store renditions as immutable outputs
steps.content: Write each completed rendition under a key containing the media version, profile, and transform version. Immutable objects make CDN caching safe and allow rollback to the previous complete encode.

component.label: Encoded Rendition Store

properties.purpose: Store complete rendition manifests and segments under deterministic versioned keys; apply lifecycle rules without deleting active content.

component.highlightReason: Separating originals and encoded outputs lets storage and retention policies match each asset's use.

steps.title: Write validated renditions
steps.content: Workers write output objects only after validation. Record checksums and profile metadata so corrupted or incomplete files never appear in a playback manifest.

connection.label: Validated media segments
connection.description: Write immutable outputs and verify checksums before marking a profile complete.

steps.title: Add the rendition catalog
steps.content: The catalog maps a media version to its ready profiles, manifests, and object keys. It is the read model for playback, not the storage location of video bytes.

component.label: Rendition Catalog

properties.purpose: Expose only checksum-verified, complete renditions for a specific media and processing version.

component.highlightReason: A separate catalog prevents playback clients from guessing object keys or seeing partial encodes.

steps.title: Publish a rendition only after validation
steps.content: A worker commits the catalog entry after every selected profile and manifest is verified. The catalog should point to the exact immutable object version that passed validation.

connection.label: Verified profile publication
connection.description: Commit ready rendition references only after checksum and manifest validation.

steps.title: Choose the publication boundary
steps.content: A worker callback is not proof of a playable asset. Require the expected profile set, checksums, and manifest validation before changing catalog state to ready; retain the prior ready version during re-encoding.

decision.question: When should a video become playable?
decision.chosen: Only after the versioned manifest and every advertised rendition have passed validation
decision.chosenReason: This avoids exposing partial encodes while preserving rollback to the last complete version.

alternatives.option: Publish as soon as the source upload completes
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast visibility, but playback may advertise renditions that do not exist yet.

alternatives.option: Replace the current catalog row during encoding
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler writes, but a failed re-encode can make the last good version unavailable.

properties.purpose: Expose only checksum-verified, complete renditions for a specific media and processing version. Expose a version only after its manifest and advertised rendition objects pass validation; keep the last ready version during re-encoding.

steps.title: Add a media event stream
steps.content: Metadata changes, completed renditions, and watch events have different consumers. A durable event stream lets indexing and recommendation jobs consume committed facts without joining the synchronous upload or playback path.

component.label: Media & Viewing Events
component.description: Committed catalog changes and privacy-scoped watch events

properties.purpose: Distribute versioned media and viewing events to independent index and recommendation consumers.

component.highlightReason: Separate consumers can rebuild indexes or recommendations from durable, replayable events.

steps.title: Publish media metadata changes
steps.content: Emit an idempotent event after the metadata commit. Consumers can reconcile against the source-of-truth version if delivery is duplicated or delayed.

connection.label: Committed media changes
connection.description: Versioned events for catalog indexing and downstream media workflows.

steps.title: Emit processing completion events
steps.content: Consumers learn that a rendition is ready from the committed catalog version, not from a transient worker heartbeat. Failed jobs emit status separately and remain retryable.

connection.label: Verified media-ready event
connection.description: Notify downstream consumers only after the catalog publication boundary.

steps.title: Add a playback entitlement service
steps.content: Copyright and DRM decisions are authorization decisions, not just CDN cache settings. Check account entitlement, territory, device policy, and rights windows before issuing a short-lived manifest or license decision.

component.label: Playback Entitlement & DRM
component.description: Rights, subscription, territory, and device checks

properties.purpose: Validate rights and subscription policy before issuing a short-lived playback manifest or DRM license decision; support bounded takedown propagation.

component.highlightReason: The prompt requires copyright protection and DRM; an explicit authorization boundary makes that requirement assessable.

steps.title: Authorize manifest requests
steps.content: The API passes the authenticated viewer and media identity to the entitlement service. Do not let a cached private manifest bypass an expired subscription, takedown, or territorial restriction.

connection.label: Viewer and rights check
connection.description: Authorize the requested media before returning a playback manifest.

steps.title: Read only published renditions
steps.content: The entitlement service resolves a ready catalog version and its supported profiles. If no complete version exists, return a clear processing state instead of a broken stream.

connection.label: Ready manifest lookup
connection.description: Resolve a rights-approved media version and its validated rendition set.

steps.title: Add global edge delivery
steps.content: A globally distributed CDN serves immutable segments near viewers and absorbs popular-release bursts. The origin remains authoritative; CDN eviction must never be the only recovery mechanism.

component.label: Global Video CDN
component.description: Regional delivery for manifests and immutable segments

properties.purpose: Deliver authorized manifests and versioned video segments near viewers; protect origins during releases and support bounded rights-cache invalidation.

component.highlightReason: Global delivery and release peaks make a cache hierarchy necessary for the stated concurrency target.

steps.title: Issue short-lived, cache-safe playback access
steps.content: Return a signed manifest or scoped playback token only after rights checks. Cache immutable public segments aggressively, but bind protected content to authorization and provide a revocation path.

connection.label: Authorized manifest and token
connection.description: Deliver a short-lived, rights-scoped playback reference for CDN retrieval.

steps.title: Request media segments at the edge
steps.content: Playback clients request the manifest's versioned segments from the CDN. The device selects the next compatible rendition based on decoder support and observed bandwidth.

connection.label: Adaptive playback requests
connection.description: Fetch authorized manifest and video segments from a nearby edge.

steps.title: Stream segments to web viewers
steps.content: The CDN returns the selected manifest and media segments. Keep segment keys immutable so cache entries cannot cross video versions or entitlement scopes.

connection.label: Adaptive video segments
connection.description: Return the authorized bitrate rendition selected by the web player.

steps.title: Support mobile and TV playback
steps.content: The same edge serves mobile and connected devices, while manifest capabilities advertise only compatible formats and DRM modes.

connection.label: Device playback requests
connection.description: Fetch a compatible, authorized rendition manifest and segments.

steps.title: Return segments to mobile and TV clients
steps.content: Clients adapt quality using measured network conditions. Keep startup work small: resolve entitlement and manifest quickly, then fetch segments in parallel from the edge.

connection.label: Device-ready video segments
connection.description: Return the selected rendition to the mobile or connected-device player.

steps.title: Protect the under-two-second startup budget
steps.content: Treat startup as a measured end-to-end budget: manifest authorization, catalog lookup, DNS/TLS, and first-segment delivery. Cache safe metadata and warm popular segments, but never trade away a required rights check.

decision.question: How should the player meet the startup target without weakening DRM?
decision.chosen: Keep the authorization and manifest path short, then serve versioned segments from nearby CDN edges
decision.chosenReason: The CDN absorbs bulk bytes while rights checks remain explicit and measurable.

alternatives.option: Proxy every video byte through the API service
alternatives.tradeoff: Centralizes policy, but couples user latency and API capacity to large media transfers.
May improve hits, but can serve content after rights or subscription changes.

properties.purpose: Deliver authorized manifests and versioned video segments near viewers; protect origins during releases and support bounded rights-cache invalidation. Prioritize nearby first-segment delivery and immutable segment caching; keep private manifest TTL short and invalidate on rights changes.

steps.title: Add a content search index
steps.content: Search needs a query-optimized index, but the metadata store remains canonical. Indexing is asynchronous and exposes freshness so a newly published video can be temporarily absent without corrupting ownership or rights state.

component.label: Video Search Index
component.description: Searchable titles, descriptions, and permitted metadata

properties.purpose: Index published, rights-eligible metadata for low-latency search; refresh from versioned events and support deletion/takedown propagation.

component.highlightReason: Search is a stated functional requirement and should not overload transactional metadata reads.

steps.title: Index committed media changes
steps.content: The search consumer checks media version and publication state before updating the index. Deletions, privacy changes, and takedowns must remove or suppress stale results.

connection.label: Versioned search updates
connection.description: Build and remove search documents from committed media events.

steps.title: Return search results through the API
steps.content: The API applies viewer visibility and rights rules to results. The search index improves retrieval speed but must not become an authorization authority.

connection.label: Ranked search results
connection.description: Return indexed candidates for authorization-aware response assembly.

steps.title: Store profiles and watch history
steps.content: Keep account preferences, playback progress, and watch-history records durable and scoped to the viewer. Make repeated progress writes idempotent and expose deletion and retention controls.

component.label: Profiles & Watch History
component.description: Viewer preferences and resumable playback state

properties.purpose: Own viewer profile, preferences, and resumable watch-history state with privacy, retention, and account-deletion semantics.

component.highlightReason: Profiles and watch history are explicit product requirements and feed personalization.

steps.title: Read and update viewer state
steps.content: Profile and watch-progress calls pass through the authenticated API. Do not put sensitive viewer identifiers into public CDN cache keys or analytics events.

connection.label: Profile and progress state
connection.description: Read viewer preferences and persist resumable watch progress.

steps.title: Record privacy-scoped viewing events
steps.content: The API emits watch events after validating the viewer and media. Keep event identity pseudonymous where possible and honor opt-out, retention, and deletion policy before using behavior for recommendations.

connection.label: Privacy-scoped watch events
connection.description: Asynchronous playback behavior for recommendation features, with retention and opt-out controls.

steps.title: Add recommendation serving
steps.content: The recommendation service combines eligible catalog candidates with permitted viewer history. Return a bounded result set and fall back to popular or editorial picks if personalization is unavailable.

component.label: Video Recommendations
component.description: Personalized candidate ranking with a safe fallback

properties.purpose: Rank rights-eligible published videos from permitted watch-history signals and provide a non-personalized fallback when unavailable.

component.highlightReason: Recommendations are required, but their failure must not block search or playback.

steps.title: Build recommendations from committed events
steps.content: The service consumes watch behavior asynchronously and reconciles against current catalog and rights state before returning any candidate.

connection.label: Eligible viewing signals
connection.description: Feed recommendation features without coupling the playback request to event processing.

steps.title: Use viewer history for relevance
steps.content: Personalization reads only the fields needed for ranking and must respect profile visibility, retention, and deletion. A history-store outage falls back to non-personalized results.

connection.label: Allowed profile features
connection.description: Read privacy-scoped preferences and history for ranking.

steps.title: Serve bounded recommendations
steps.content: The API returns a small ranked list independently from the manifest path. A slow ranker should time out to a safe fallback rather than delay playback startup.

connection.label: Ranked video candidates
connection.description: Return a bounded, rights-eligible recommendation list to the API.

steps.title: Keep recommendations out of the playback critical path
steps.content: Search and recommendation failures should degrade their own panels only. Manifest authorization and segment delivery remain available even when indexing or ranking is delayed.

decision.question: What happens when the recommendation service is slow?
decision.chosen: Apply a short timeout and return a safe non-personalized list
decision.chosenReason: Recommendations improve discovery but are not required to start a video.

alternatives.option: Wait for ranking before returning the playback page
alternatives.tradeoff: May improve ranking freshness but violates the startup budget when the model is slow.
Couples a non-critical discovery feature to playback availability.

properties.purpose: Rank rights-eligible published videos from permitted watch-history signals and provide a non-personalized fallback when unavailable. Return ranked candidates within a bounded timeout; fall back safely without blocking search results or playback.

steps.title: Add pipeline and delivery monitoring
steps.content: Track upload verification failures, queue age, encode completion, rendition integrity, startup latency, CDN hit ratio, rights denials, and storage/egress cost. Use viewer-facing SLOs rather than worker CPU alone.

component.label: Video Platform Observability
component.description: Playback, processing, rights, and cost signals

properties.purpose: Observe startup latency, CDN delivery, queue age, failed encodes, rights decisions, storage integrity, and egress cost.

component.highlightReason: A system can have healthy workers while viewers experience slow startup or broken renditions.

steps.title: Observe processing failures
steps.content: Alert on growing queue age, retry exhaustion, failed checksums, and time from verified upload to playable catalog state.

connection.label: Encode health and backlog
connection.description: Report processing latency, failures, retries, and rendition integrity.

steps.title: Observe viewer delivery
steps.content: Measure startup p95, first-segment latency, rebuffering, cache hit ratio, origin load, and rights-related cache invalidations by region and device.

connection.label: Regional playback telemetry
connection.description: Measure viewer experience and CDN/origin health during normal and release traffic.

steps.title: Plan for popular releases
steps.content: Use release schedules and observed audience demand to pre-warm eligible immutable segments, reserve encoding capacity, and protect origin limits. Scale from measured concurrency and regional cache misses; the brief says millions of viewers but does not specify a precise peak multiplier.

scaleTrigger.metric: Concurrent viewers, startup p95, CDN miss rate, and origin saturation
scaleTrigger.action: Pre-warm popular segments and scale edge/origin and worker capacity from measured demand
scaleTrigger.impact: Release traffic is absorbed without tying transcoding backlogs or origin overload to the playback request path.
